rfi.title: Nepal glacier disaster toll passes 1,000 as calls for climate justice grow
rfi.description: The death toll from last week's devastating Himalayan glacial floods passed 1,000 on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors. Nepal's foreign minister said the disaster was "a warning signal" of the growing risks posed by climate change.

rfi.title: DRC school year begins amid Ebola, strikes and conflict
rfi.description: Millions of students returned to school across the Democratic Republic of Congo on Tuesday, but the new term began amid an Ebola outbreak affecting six provinces, a teachers’ strike call and continuing conflict in the east. In AFC/M23-controlled territories, the movement organised the return to classrooms even as Kinshasa continued to pay primary and secondary school teachers.

rfi.title: French clubs cash in as Ligue 1 transfer window comes to a close
rfi.description: The transfer window for French football clubs closed on Tuesday evening after three months of trading that saw the 18 Ligue 1 sides splash out €522 million and reap €894 million in player sales.

rfi.title: French schools start new year in shadow of summer cyberattack
rfi.description: Millions of pupils are returning to classrooms across France on Tuesday for the start of the new school year, with some schools forced to fall back on paper timetables and registers after a major cyberattack disrupted education systems over the summer.

rfi.title: Russia’s return to G20 talks unsettles Europe as Iran and trade tensions loom
rfi.description: Russia's presence at the opening of G20 meetings in North Carolina sparked pushback from Europe on Monday, adding fresh tension to talks already clouded by the Iran war and US President Donald Trump's trade policies.

rfi.title: Ukraine air defences top agenda as EU ministers meet in Ireland
rfi.description: European Union defence and foreign ministers gathering in Ireland this week are set to focus on strengthening Ukraine’s air defences, as concern grows over both Russia’s intensifying bombardment and what European officials see as a widening campaign of destabilisation across the continent.

rfi.title: France takes aim at fast-fashion giants with new pricing penalties
rfi.description: France will start imposing fees on ultra-fast fashion from Tuesday, with charges set to rise to almost €20 per garment as the government steps up pressure on major Asian e-commerce platforms including Shein.

rfi.title: From labels to Netflix, how Quebec's fight to protect French collides with US trade
rfi.description: French-language protections in Quebec have emerged as an unlikely source of friction between Canada and the United States, bringing rules designed to protect French in overwhelmingly English-speaking North America into a much bigger fight over trade.

rfi.title: No more Messi nights for Argentina as skipper says adios to national squad
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino led the tributes to Argentina skipper Lionel Messi, who announced his retirement from international football just over a month after playing in the 2026 World Cup final.

rfi.title: 'Devoted servant of the nation': Former French PM Édouard Balladur dies aged 97
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Édouard Balladur died in Paris late Monday at the age of 97, his family said. Born in Turkey, he served as former president Francois Mitterrand's last prime minister from March 1993 to May 1995, carrying out several major privatisations of state companies, and unsuccessfully ran for the top job in 1995.

rfi.title: Ten years after Gabon’s post-election violence, painful questions remain
rfi.description: Ten years on, victims of violence that followed president Ali Bongo’s disputed re-election in Gabon are still demanding truth and justice. Questions also remain over the possible involvement of French nationals and the response of the French authorities.

rfi.title: Niger coup attempt: 'Russians saved the day' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Niger’s military government has survived its most serious internal challenge since seizing power in 2023, after Russian paramilitaries helped loyalist forces crush last Saturday's attempted coup in the capital, Niamey. RFI spoke to an expert who explains how this episode has left General Abdourahamane Tiani’s junta weakened and more dependent on Russia.

rfi.title: French high schools scramble to work out rules as phone ban takes effect
rfi.description: The new school year starts on Tuesday in France, and with it comes a new rule: mobile phones will no longer be allowed in high schools. The ban came into force a week before the first day of term, leaving schools with little time to work out how to put it into practice.

rfi.title: France's international photojournalism festival founder Leroy dies aged 69
rfi.description: Tributes have been pouring in for Jean-François Leroy, the founder of the Visa pour l'image photojournalism festival, who died on Monday at the age of 69.

rfi.title: UN committee presents legal case for broad slavery reparations
rfi.description: Countries are "legally obliged" to provide broad reparations for harms resulting from both direct and indirect involvement in the transatlantic African slave trade, a United Nations committee has said. This comes amid a fresh interpretation of a global accord, published on Monday.

rfi.title: What the SDF’s dissolution means for Syria’s Kurds and neighbouring Turkey
rfi.description: Nearly a week after the Syrian Democratic Forces agreed to dissolve, the consequences are beginning to take shape for Syria's Kurds and neighbouring Turkey. As the former US-backed force is absorbed into the Syrian state, questions remain over what the country's Kurds have secured in return – from language and political rights to protections for women – and what the end of more than a decade of Kurdish-led autonomy means for Turkey's own conflict with Kurdish militants.

rfi.title: Dissident militia in Colombia says kidnapped French Foreign Legion soldier alive
rfi.description: Colombian rebels have claimed responsibility for kidnapping a Colombian soldier serving in the French Foreign Legion, saying he is alive and in good health nearly a month after he was seized in the south-west of the country. However they warned the government against any military intervention.

rfi.title: EU hides disappointment after Iceland's 'No' vote
rfi.description: The EU put a brave face Sunday on Iceland's vote against restarting membership talks, but the outcome was a bitter pill to swallow – robbing Brussels of a hoped-for success story while delighting its eurosceptic critics.

euronews.title: What's behind France's plan to survey school children on sexual violence?
euronews.description: For the first time, France's annual school questionnaire on bullying — which has been handed out to pupils since 2023 — will include questions on sexual violence. euronews.title: Spanish government approves €309 million aid package for Ceuta amid migrant crisis
euronews.description: Spain's Economy Minister said the aid package represents a 'shock response' designed to meet the demands of social organisations and the city government.

euronews.title: US launches new strikes in southern Iran, Tehran responds with attacks in Jordan
euronews.description: The US military launched new waves of strikes on military installations along Iran's southern coast. Tehran responded immediately with missile and drone attacks in Jordan, sparking a new flare-up of hostilities and threats from both sides.

euronews.title: Ryanair's Boeing 737 stairs tied to hundreds of passenger falls, study says
euronews.description: Ryanair's Boeing 737 comes with retractable onboard stairs that cut costs and turnaround times, but an Italian safety study has linked them to hundreds of passenger falls since 2021.

euronews.title: SCO challenges West as diverse group of nations pursues multipolar future
euronews.description: The summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, which represents almost half of the world’s population, ended with an aim to signal the rise of a global powerhouse challenging the West. Yet the SCO's diversity also revealed significant disagreements and divergent interests.

euronews.title: Von der Leyen pledges response to Russian hybrid attacks ahead of Rutte meeting
euronews.description: As Germany formally blames Russia for a hybrid warfare incident involving an explosive-laden drone at one of its airports, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will meet NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte to discuss a coordinated response.

euronews.title: Russia's Starlink copycat has failed so far but still threatens Ukraine
euronews.description: Russia's homegrown Starlink rival has suffered a fresh setback, with an entire batch of satellites failing to reach orbit — but even a partially working system could still sharpen Russian strikes on Ukraine.

euronews.title: Brussels says €90 billion loan for Ukraine is enough for now amid growing doubts
euronews.description: The longevity of the EU's €90 billion support loan for Ukraine is in serious doubt as Russia escalates the war and drives up material costs. Brussels says the financial plan remains sufficient "for the moment".

euronews.title: Russia behind attempted drone 'attack' at Leipzig airport, Berlin says
euronews.description: Germany has for months reported suspicious drone sightings over military and industrial sites, but an incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport on the night of 4-5 August raised the alarm as a drone found there carried explosives.

euronews.title: EU’s green fashion rules face test as global emissions rise 6.3%
euronews.description: The findings of a report on fashion data pose a political challenge for the EU, which has made textiles one of the testing grounds for its broader push to move from a linear economy – make, sell and throw away – towards a circular one.

euronews.title: GPHG 2026: Our favourite luxury timepieces vying for top watch industry awards
euronews.description: The Grand Prix d'Horlogerie has revealed its much anticipated official nominations for this year's edition and world tour and here are eight models you should be watching out for.

euronews.title: Shein and Temu items could face €20 levy in France’s crackdown on ultra-fast fashion
euronews.description: Imports of small parcels from China have already fallen by up to 40 per cent since a separate €3 EU levy came into force in July.

euronews.title: Thailand confirms it will cut visa-free stays to 30 days for EU travellers
euronews.description: Travellers from EU countries will have less time to explore Thailand without a visa from 15 September, as the popular holiday destination halves its current 60-day allowance.

euronews.title: EU to gather ‘brightest minds’ to boost defence as Russia threat grows
euronews.description: The EU is setting up a high-level group of political and military leaders from member states, Ukraine and the UK to speed up efforts to close Europe's defence capability gaps amid rising Russian threats.

euronews.title: ESA's BepiColombo mission nears major turning point on Mercury approach
euronews.description: The European Space Agency's (ESA) BepiColombo mission to the planet Mercury faces its most critical manoeuvre yet, as a pair of probes drop off the mothership on their way to one of the solar system's most extreme places.

euronews.title: Iran says it will return to June ceasefire deal if US does the same
euronews.description: Iran's President Pezeshkian made the offer at the SCO summit in Bishkek hours after Iran and the US exchanged fire over the weekend. IRGC's demands for control of Hormuz and war compensation remain conditions Washington is unlikely to accept.

euronews.title: UK records hottest summer on record, Met Office says
euronews.description: According to a study carried out by Met Office scientists, the record-breaking season was made roughly 130 times more likely due to "human-induced climate change."

lemonde.description: Avant même son arrivée au pouvoir, en juillet, le dirigeant travailliste avait fait savoir qu’il était favorable à un plus grand contrôle de l’Etat, en particulier dans la distribution d’eau, secteur où la principale compagnie, Thames Water, est en grande difficulté financière.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : souverainisme et air conditionné, les deux piliers de Marine Le Pen et du RN pour lutter contre le dérèglement climatique
lemonde.description: « Les candidats face au climat » (1/5). Le Rassemblement national et Marine Le Pen défendent une version « positive » de l’écologie centrée sur la réindustrialisation de la France et le déploiement de la climatisation, des propositions au chiffrage pour le moment obscur.

lemonde.title: Syrie : les infrastructures découvertes à Deir ez-Zor sont « conformes à celles d’un réacteur nucléaire », selon l’AIEA
lemonde.description: A la mi-août, l’autorité de sûreté nucléaire et le gouvernement syrien avaient annoncé la découverte de « quelques tonnes de matières nucléaires » sur un site « non déclaré », « héritage de l’ancien régime ».

lemonde.title: Au Venezuela, l’Assemblée nationale approuve l’accord pétrolier avec les Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: L’accord permet aux Etats-Unis d’exploiter 17 gisements pétroliers vénézuéliens dont le potentiel est évalué à 65 milliards de barils. Le Venezuela évalue à 209 milliards de dollars la création de richesse sur vingt-cinq ans.

lemonde.title: Juan Branco : le parquet de Paris requiert le renvoi en procès de l’avocat pour viol
lemonde.description: Dans un document de 32 pages daté du 6 août, le parquet de Paris demande également un non-lieu pour d’autres faits d’agression sexuelle et de viol sur deux autres femmes, pour lesquels l’avocat est également poursuivi.

lemonde.title: Inondations dans l’Himalaya : le bilan dépasse désormais le millier de morts au Népal
lemonde.description: Les autorités népalaises et chinoises sont toujours sans nouvelles de près de 4 500 personnes, six jours après la catastrophe.

lemonde.title: Guerre au Soudan : une seconde base des paramilitaires des FSR identifiée en Ethiopie, signe de l’implication croissante du premier ministre, Abiy Ahmed
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement d’Addis-Abeba fournit, en toute discrétion, un soutien logistique et militaire de plus en plus important aux paramilitaires soudanais, menaçant de faire basculer la guerre civile au Soudan en un conflit régional.

lemonde.title: En Guinée-Bissau, le passage à un régime présidentiel fort approuvé par référendum
lemonde.description: Le scrutin, qui s’est déroulé dimanche dans un climat politique tendu, précède de quelques mois les élections générales prévues le 6 décembre pour un retour des civils au pouvoir. L’opposition avait appelé à le boycotter.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : accord avec le FMI en vue d'un programme d'aide de plus de 2 milliards de dollars

observador.description: Centenas reuniram-se na Plaza de África com velas. Na quarta-feira, 2 de setembro — o "Dia de Ceuta" — espera-se uma manifestação de maior dimensão, convocada por associações de moradores.

observador.title: Arquitetos paisagistas chumbam mina de caulino em Peniche
observador.description: 471 dos 662 sobreiros inventariados serão abatidos, mas o plano de recuperação não prevê plantar um único. Consulta pública da AIA encerrou esta terça-feira.

observador.title: Quem pode usar bens apreendidos pelas polícias e para quê?
observador.description: Lei permite que o Estado use bens apreendidos em operações antes de haver condenação em tribunal. Mas o que é a "utilidade operacional" e quem pode usar? Entenda as regras e exceções em seis pontos.

observador.title: Berlim acusa Rússia de ataque em Leipzig e promete respostas
observador.description: Ataque com drone em Leipzig foi coordenado pela Rússia, concluiu Berlim, que respondeu com o encerramento de consulado e centro cultural. NATO e UE reúnem na quarta para debater guerra híbrida.

observador.title: Russia dá ultimato à Arménia sobre entrada na União Europeia
observador.description: Putin considera que a Arménia não pode pertencer à União Europeia e à União Eurasiática, formada por países da ex-URSS. O Presidente russo ameaçou ajustar as "políticas comerciais e económicas".

observador.title: Moçambique. PS questiona Governo sobre linha de 500 milhões
observador.description: José Luís Carneiro, em visita a Maputo, promete pergunta parlamentar ao Ministério das Finanças sobre a linha de crédito acordada em dezembro, na Cimeira do Porto.

observador.title: Homem detido por matar companheira em Albufeira
observador.description: O casal, de nacionalidade britânica, estava acompanhado de uma criança. A GNR deteve o homem e a PJ assumiu a investigação.

observador.title: Cheque-livro: 85,9% de taxa de utilização na 2.ª edição
observador.description: Ministério da Cultura celebra subida da taxa de utilização para 85,9% e mais 14,8% de vouchers usados face à 1.ª edição. Continuidade do programa ainda por decidir.

observador.title: 22h. Médio Oriente. Irão retalia após ataques dos EUA
observador.description: Teerão fala de uma “operação decisiva das forças armadas iranianas”. Ainda, secretário-geral do PS pede ao primeiro-ministro que não dê razão aos "efeitos pirotécnicos" do Chega sobre Luís Neves.

observador.title: Zelensky: espaço aéreo russo "extremamente perigoso"
observador.description: O Presidente ucraniano dirigiu o aviso a companhias aéreas, seguradoras e aeroportos de Moscovo e São Petersburgo. Kiev nunca tinha feito uma ameaça de superioridade aérea sobre a Rússia.

observador.title: Irão ameaça EUA com "resposta militar" ao bloqueio
observador.description: O presidente do parlamento iraniano avisou que Teerão responderá militarmente se o bloqueio naval dos EUA se agravar. Estreito de Ormuz no centro da tensão após colapso do cessar-fogo de junho.

observador.title: Catedral de São Paulo será palco de eventos de clube noturno
observador.description: Catedral já foi palco de concertos no passado, mas passa a ser parceiro exclusivo do clube noturno Fabric. Primeiro evento será no dia 29 de outubro e programa inclui artistas de diferentes áreas.

observador.title: Época balnear: 22 mortos e 1.285 salvamentos
observador.description: Durante os quatro meses que correspondem à época balnear foram registadas 22 mortes nas praias, 12 delas por afogamento. Para além das mortes há ainda um banhista desaparecido desde 28 de agosto.

observador.title: Angola prepara projeto Nature4Health para prevenir pandemias
observador.description: O projeto Nature4Health, financiado pelo PNUD e pela Alemanha, quer proteger a saúde pública pela conservação da natureza. Implementação prevista até ao fim de 2027.

observador.title: Le Pen lidera sondagens para as presidenciais de 2027
observador.description: Com Le Pen a rondar os 34% na primeira volta, Philippe e Mélenchon disputam o segundo lugar. À esquerda, uma "verdadeira fragmentação" complica qualquer estratégia de vitória.

observador.title: Polícia Marítima resgata 33 pessoas durante missão na Grécia
observador.description: A Polícia Marítima portuguesa está em missão na ilha de Gavdos, na Grécia. As autoridades portuguesas, a pedido das autoridades gregas resgataram 33 pessoas, entre elas alguns menores.

observador.title: Gül no Galatasaray, Porto arrecada até 11M€
observador.description: Avançado turco de 22 anos somou 71 jogos e nove golos pelos dragões em duas épocas. Turcos podem ainda pagar mais 1 milhão em variáveis.

spiegel.title: Anschlag in Leipzig: Putin verurteilt Berlins Strafmaßnahmen gegen Russland
spiegel.description: Nach dem Fund einer nicht explodierten Sprengstoffdrohne auf dem Flughafen Leipzig/Halle verkündet die Bundesregierung Sanktionen gegen Russland. Nun reagiert Kremlchef Putin.

spiegel.title: USA bombardiert nahe Straße von Hormus, Iran startet Vergeltungsangriffe
spiegel.description: Das US-Militär bombardiert erneut in Iran – Präsident Trump spricht von »großen und gewaltigen« Angriffen. Iranische Medien berichten indes, dass dabei eine Hochzeitsfeier getroffen worden sei.

spiegel.title: Brandenburg: Anschlag auf Stromleitungen – mögliche linksextreme Hintergründe im Fokus
spiegel.description: In Brandenburg sollten selbst gebaute Flugkörper im Stile von Silvesterraketen ein Umspannwerk lahmlegen. Die Sicherheitsbehörden sind nervös. Die Konstruktion erforderte zwar kein Spezialistenwissen, war jedoch aufwendig.

spiegel.title: DFB-Pokal: BVB gewinnt 5:0 gegen Fünftligisten aus Hamburg
spiegel.description: Die Eimsbütteler Sensation, sie ist ausgeblieben. Eine halbe Stunde stemmte sich der Hamburger Oberligist HEBC erfolgreich gegen Borussia Dortmund, dann setzte sich der Vizemeister doch deutlich durch.

spiegel.title: Russland: Wie Deutschland auf hybride Angriffe reagieren will
spiegel.description: Friedrich Merz droht, vollstrecken müssen andere: Alexander Dobrindt und Johann Wadephul erklären am Dienstag, wie Deutschland auf hybride Angriffe aus Russland reagiert. So richtig wohl fühlen sie sich dabei nicht.

spiegel.title: Wolodymyr Selenskyj warnt Airlines vor Flügen über Russland
spiegel.description: Nach heftigen russischen Luftangriffen wendet sich Selenskyj mit einer Warnung an Fluggesellschaften, die weiter über Russland fliegen. Kremlchef Wladimir Putin reagierte noch in der Nacht.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Sorgt der Iran-Krieg für einen Boom der Solarenergie? - Podcast
spiegel.description: Der Irankrieg treibt die Ölpreise nach oben. Gleichzeitig boomt die Solarenergie. Was dahintersteckt, erklärt US-Korrespondent Claus Hecking im Podcast.

spiegel.title: Flughafen Leipzig/Halle: Wie Berlin auf Putins Schattenkrieg reagiert
spiegel.description: Die Bundesregierung hat Russland als Drahtzieher hinter der Drohnenattacke auf dem Leipziger Flughafen benannt. Eine weitere Eskalation vermeidet sie aus guten Gründen.

spiegel.title: Dänemark: Männer über 55 Jahren haben künftig keinen Anspruch mehr auf Fruchtbarkeitsbehandlungen
spiegel.description: Bisher galt in dem skandinavischen Land nur für Frauen eine Altersgrenze bei Fruchtbarkeitsbehandlungen, nun zieht Dänemark bei Männern nach. Die zuständige Behörde verweist auf Forschungsergebnisse.

spiegel.title: Nationalspieler Nick Woltemade wechselt zu Juventus Turin: Eine Flucht mit Jürgen Klopps Segen
spiegel.description: Nach nur einer Saison in England zieht Nick Woltemade weiter nach Italien. Ein Grund: Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen hat ihm Newcastles Coach mitgeteilt, dass er auf andere Stürmer setzt. Und dann ist da noch der neue Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp.

spiegel.title: Pharmakonzern Novartis stoppt nach Todesfällen mehrere Studien
spiegel.description: In der Schweiz sind drei Studienteilnehmer bei einer experimentellen Zelltherapie gestorben – offenbar an einer bekannten Komplikation. Novartis hat nun mehrere Studien ausgesetzt.

spiegel.title: Anschlag Leipzig: Nato begrüßt Maßnahmen, Grüne fordern härtere Sanktionen gegen Russland
spiegel.description: Wegen des versuchten Angriffs in Leipzig hat die Bundesregierung mehrere Maßnahmen gegen Russland angekündigt. Partnerländer der Nato stellen sich neben die Regierung, die konkrete Reaktion aus dem Kreml ist noch abzuwarten.

spiegel.title: Hitzetote im Sommer in Deutschland: Ein Bestatter aus Köln zieht Bilanz
spiegel.description: Überhitzte Wohnungen, überforderte Pflegeheime und zahlreiche Tote, für die aber Kühlzellen in Bestattungsunternehmen fehlen: Der Sommer 2026 zeigt, wie schnell die Bestattungsinfrastruktur an ihre Grenzen gerät.

spiegel.title: Nepal: Schulleiter rettet 900 Kinder vor Sturzflut im Himalaja
spiegel.description: Als Rajendra Dawadi seine Schule in Nepal verließ, lief das Wasser schon ins Gebäude. Doch da hatte der Schulleiter bereits dafür gesorgt, dass Hunderte Kinder in Sicherheit waren. Hier erzählt er vom Tag der Flutkatastrophe.

spiegel.title: Meinung – Polen: Wie Präsident Karol Nawrocki die Deutschen sieht - ein Kommentar
spiegel.description: Polens Staatsoberhaupt Karol Nawrocki findet: Den Deutschen ist auch 87 Jahre nach dem Überfall auf sein Land nicht zu trauen. Außerdem will er Reparationen, es droht ein Zerwürfnis an Europas Ostflanke.

spiegel.title: Polizei stoppt überladenen Tiertransporter in Oberbayern
spiegel.description: 190 Jungtiere auf engstem Raum, teils so eng gedrängt, dass ihre Rücken an die Decke stießen: Das hat die oberbayerische Polizei bei der Kontrolle eines Tiertransporters entdeckt.

spiegel.title: Flughafen Leipzig/Halle: Bundesregierung spricht von hybrider Kriegsführung
spiegel.description: Die Bundesregierung sieht einen russischen Geheimdienst als Urheber des versuchten Sprengstoffanschlags auf den Leipziger Flughafen. Die wichtigsten Aussagen von Innenminister Dobrindt und Außenminister Wadephul im Video.

spiegel.title: SPIEGEL TV-Reporter im Deep Dive: Wie bleibt man ruhig, wenn es gefährlich wird?
spiegel.description: Neonazis, Identitäre, Clankriminalität: Thomas Heise und Henrik Neumann von SPIEGEL TV recherchieren, wo andere lieber Abstand halten. Hier stellen sie sich exklusiv Ihren Fragen.

elpais.title: Madrid acusa al Gobierno de “boicotear” la concentración por Ceuta pese a que el Ejecutivo permitirá que se celebre
elpais.description: La Delegación de Gobierno explica que el Consistorio no es titular del derecho de reunión, pero dará cobertura a la concentración como acto institucional: “No existe ninguna prohibición”

elpais.title: Bruselas ve “intentos de Rusia de sacar partido” de la crisis de Ceuta, pero afirma que no hay “pruebas” de que la provocara
elpais.description: La Comisión Europea afirma que no puede afirmar que el origen de la crisis esté en “desinformación procedente de actores estatales extranjeros”

elpais.title: Nervios y miedo entre familias migrantes acampadas en las calles de Ceuta: “Damos vueltas para encontrar dónde dormir”
elpais.description: Jóvenes que duermen en el polígono de El Tarajal aseguran que les están tirando sus pertenencias y varias mujeres cuentan que les han dicho que se tienen que ir el jueves

elpais.title: El Gobierno aprueba un plan de 309 millones para despejar la idea del “abandono” de Ceuta
elpais.description: El Ejecutivo sostiene que las relaciones con la Casa Real “son buenas” y no teme la reacción de Marruecos ante la visita del Rey a la ciudad autónoma

elpais.title: Alemania acusa a Rusia del ataque fallido con drones bomba en Leipzig
elpais.description: La policía halla explosivos y cohetes caseros en una subestación eléctrica clave para el funcionamiento de la mayor central térmica de Brandeburgo

elpais.title: Guerra híbrida contra Europa
elpais.description: Alemania señala a Rusia por un intento de atentado con drones que marca una nueva dimensión en los ataques en territorio de la UE

elpais.title: La guerra híbrida de Rusia en suelo europeo se acelera un 50% desde abril
elpais.description: En nueve meses de 2026 se han registrado 50 violaciones del espacio aéreo de la UE con drones y aeronaves, frente a 62 en los cuatro años anteriores

elpais.title: Estados Unidos vuelve a bombardear Irán, que responde con ataques contra sus efectivos en Jordania
elpais.description: Trump asegura que la negociación “es papel mojado” y amenaza con “mayores ataques” si Teherán responde

elpais.title: La marcha del secretario del Ejército de Tierra descabeza una fuerza clave del Pentágono en plena guerra de Irán
elpais.description: La dimisión de Dan Driscoll llega después de meses de enfrentamientos con el secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth, y se suma a un largo elenco de salidas de altos mandos

elpais.title: Judeline se convierte en la primera mujer española en alcanzar el número uno mundial en Spotify
elpais.description: La gaditana llega al ‘Top 50 Global’ con ‘BbY WOW’, su colaboración con Karol G y Rusowsky, y supera un techo que solo había rozado Rosalía

elpais.title: Messi, el rey que abdica
elpais.description: Leo nos enseñó, en cámara lenta, cómo es la esencia del fútbol. Caminando. Vagando por la cancha como si le perteneciera manejando los tiempos como un reloj y la pelota como un objeto sagrado

elpais.title: Discreto, accesible, sin ostentaciones y con una gestoría en Marbella: cae el asesor fiscal que los narcos se recomendaban en la Costa del Sol
elpais.description: La Policía Nacional arresta por segunda vez a un especialista en blanqueo de dinero que trabajaba para varias organizaciones criminales

elpais.title: El jurado del caso de Lindsay Clancy no logra llegar a un veredicto unánime y el juez ordena seguir deliberando
elpais.description: La enfermera de Massachusetts se enfrenta a una vida en la cárcel o el ingreso en un centro psiquiátrico tras asesinar a sus tres hijos

elpais.title: Keri Russell y Matthew Rhys: de un amor secreto que se destapó gracias a un robo a ser la pareja más poderosa de la tele
elpais.description: En Hollywood, donde cada romance parece destinado a copar titulares, ellos han conseguido mantener el suyo lejos de los focos. Más de una década juntos, tres hijos en común y cinco nominaciones a los Emmy solo en esta edición avalan a una de las parejas más sólidas de la televisión

elpais.title: Se desploman dos plantas del Palacio de los Hurtado de Mendoza de Almazán, declarado Bien de Interés Cultural
elpais.description: El derrumbe ha abierto un enorme boquete en la fachada del edificio, y ha afectado también a parte de su galería gótica

elpais.title: Los interesados en comprar el polémico ático de la Comunidad de Madrid no pueden visitarlo
elpais.description: El Gobierno de Ayuso ha subido una nota a la web aclarando dudas en la que también indica que la terraza, originalmente de 200 metros, fue reducida a la mitad

elpais.title: Mazón rechaza la relación causal entre el retraso del envío del Es-Alert y las víctimas
elpais.description: Argumenta que no era el responsable de adoptar medidas de prevención y no participó en la redacción de la alerta

elpais.title: La Fiscalía se opone a las quejas de Ábalos y Koldo contra la sentencia del Supremo: “Están abocadas al fracaso”
elpais.description: Aldama también pide al alto tribunal que desestime los incidentes de nulidad presentados por el exministro de Transportes y su exasesor

nyt.title: U.S. Strikes Iran Over Strait of Hormuz Mines, Trump Says
nyt.description: U.S. Central Command did not say precisely what it was trying to destroy in Iran, but it said the attacks were aimed at Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps.

nyt.title: Two More Oil Tankers Are Attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
nyt.description: The ships were hit near Oman on Monday, the latest attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf. Oil prices rose more than 2 percent.

nyt.title: Bond Sell-Off Threatens to Squeeze Borrowers Around the World
nyt.description: Government bond yields are hitting multi-decade highs, reflecting anxiety about debt levels, deficits and inflation. The effects will extend to mortgages, business loans and other types of credit.

nyt.title: What the Jump in Global Interest Rates Means for the Economy
nyt.description: Global interest rates are rising. Interest rates on U.S. government bonds can affect everything from auto and student loans to mortgages.

nyt.title: Can JD Vance Win Over Skeptical Jewish Voters?
nyt.description: The vice president is attempting to unite conservative Jews with their antagonists in one coalition, as one appearance in Nevada on Monday showed. Some are uneasy about it.

nyt.title: House Votes to Avert Government Shutdown Before Midterm Elections
nyt.description: Lawmakers sent the legislation to President Trump in an overwhelming vote, reflecting bipartisan enthusiasm around punting a messy spending fight until after the midterms.

nyt.title: Ed Markey’s Massachusetts Senate Race Is a Generational Fight, With a Twist
nyt.description: In Massachusetts, the octogenarian senator Ed Markey faces a challenge from a much younger centrist, Representative Seth Moulton.

nyt.title: What to Watch in the Massachusetts Primary Election
nyt.description: Senator Edward Markey, who began his congressional career in 1976, faces a challenge from Representative Seth Moulton.

nyt.title: Woman Killed in Times Square Stabbing Identified as Bank of America VP
nyt.description: The New York Police Department made public the names of some of the people involved in a seemingly random knife attack on a crowded Manhattan street, but questions remained.

nyt.title: On Trump’s Ballroom, Chief Justice Finds Himself in an Unusual Spot: In Dissent
nyt.description: Chief Justice John G. Roberts Jr. has been in the majority in divided cases more times than any other chief since 1953. But not this time.

nyt.title: China or the U.S.? Two Meetings Offer Competing Showcases of Global Power.
nyt.description: As Xi Jinping gathered with the leaders of Russia and Iran, Europe challenged the Trump administration at the G20, offering a split-screen view of a changing world.

nyt.title: Carney Tells Trump Officials to ‘Stop Throwing Shade’ Over Canada-U.S. Trade Talks
nyt.description: Amid a trade war, Canada’s Liberals swept three special votes and new polling suggested strong support for Prime Minister Mark Carney and his retaliatory tariffs against the U.S.

nyt.title: Lindsay Clancy Trial: Jury Deliberations Will Stretch Into 5th Day
nyt.description: Jurors have now deliberated for nearly 24 hours over four days and say they are deadlocked. A judge told them to keep trying to reach a verdict.

nyt.title: Why MAHA Rallied for a Mother Seeking Alternative Treatments for Her Son’s Cancer
nyt.description: Dayna Mooney chose alternative remedies over the recommendations of her son’s doctors. Was that her right as a parent or a threat to his care?

nyt.title: Was John Galliano Ever Really Canceled? Not by the Fashion Crowd.
nyt.description: This may be the end of the Costume Institute’s John Galliano exhibition, but it’s not likely to be the end of his career.

nyt.title: Nepal’s Economy Has Few Ways to Absorb the Cost of Flood Damage
nyt.description: The country’s government estimates that the recent catastrophic floods caused $5 billion in damage. That’s one-tenth of Nepal’s entire economy.

nyt.title: How to Help Nepal Flash Flood Victims
nyt.description: More than 1,000 people have been killed in a Himalayan landslide and flooding, and thousands more are missing. Here’s how you can help.

nyt.title: A New World Order Is Coming. We Aren’t Ready.
nyt.description: We must be honest about the seriousness of the situation we’re in.

republika.description: Al tecnico dei lombardi non basta battere una squadra della massima serie. Granata battuti in casa dal Monza

republika.description: Dopo l’indagine sui droni a Lipsia è arrivato il provvedimento del governo tedesco, a lungo rimandato dopo l’invasione dell’Ucraina per il valore strategico dell’ambasciata

republika.title: Elly Schlein: "Le Primarie? Smettiamola di parlare di noi e pensiamo ai problemi della gente”
republika.description: La segretaria del Pd alla Festa dell’Unità di Genova arriva con la sindaca Salis: “Meloni chiusa nel palazzo, sulla legge elettorale mossa della disperazione”

republika.description: Dopo settimane di indagini, l’accusa del governo Merz che chiude la Casa russa a Berlino e il consolato di Bonn. Von der Leyen e Rutte: “Ci saranno conseguenze”. La minaccia di Putin: “Non hanno le prove, reagiremo”

republika.title: Melonellum, emendamento opposizione per preferenze libere. Schlein: ballottaggio mossa disperata
republika.description: Scaduto il termine per la presentazione delle proposte di modifica in commissione: solo tre sono firmate da tutto il centrodestra

republika.description: La tragedia ad Apice, nel Beneventano. Secondo la ricostruzione, a sparare è stato Gianni Licciardi: ha ucciso Donato all’interno della struttura e Franco in giardino, dove poi ha rivolto l’arma contro se stesso

republika.title: Piantedosi: “Sarà espulso il migrante che ha offeso il tricolore a Firenze”
republika.description: Qualche giorno fa era stato diffuso un video in cui l’uomo staccava la bandiera italiana dal muro e la gettava a terra. E’ stato portato in un Cpr

republika.title: McTominay, aritmia benigna: lo scozzese del Napoli sarà operato, fuori almeno un mese
republika.description: Lo rende noto il club azzurro in una nota. Lo scozzese salterà Inter, Arsenal, Bologna e Fiorentina, dovrebbe tornare a ottobre dopo la sosta per le gare delle nazionali, quando al Maradona arriverà il Frosinone

republika.title: Fn di Vannacci al raduno neonazi di Camelot a Trento. Bonelli: “Piantedosi applichi legge Mancino”
republika.description: Il referente trentino del partito di Vannacci parteciperà all’evento in programma dal 3 al 6 settembre organizzato dal Veneto Fronte Skinheads che dovrebbe richiamare militanti dell’estrema destra da diversi Paesi europei

republika.title: Calabresi verso la candidatura a sindaco di Milano, si dimette dagli incarichi in Chora Media
republika.description: L’ex direttore di Repubblica e la Stampa ha lasciato il suo ruolo di direttore editoriale in Chora Media. L’annuncio ufficiale della corsa elettorale alla festa dell’Unità di Milano

republika.title: Lega Nord, nasce il comitato per il congresso: sfida a Salvini per riprendersi il simbolo
republika.description: Si è costituito il 28 agosto a Forlì. La mossa arriva nel momento più delicato per gli equilibri del Carroccio. Pini: “Non è un’operazione nostalgia”. Occhi puntati su Pontida, fissata il 20 settembre

republika.title: La sapienza di Enzo Bianchi, un profeta del dialogo segnato dall’esilio da Bose
republika.description: Il monaco scomparso oggi era stato autore di innumerevoli saggi non solo a carattere religioso, ma soprattutto umano

republika.title: Sondaggi politici, confermato il sorpasso di Vannacci su Forza Italia. Sei punti dividono FdI e Pd
republika.description: Secondo la rilevazione Swg per La7 del 31 agosto Futuro nazionale sale al 7,5% e scavalca gli azzurri di Tajani. Avs sopra la Lega, cala di poco FdI

republika.title: Addio a Enzo Bianchi, monaco che dialogava dentro e fuori la cristianità
republika.description: Aveva 83 anni, aveva fondato nel 1965 la comunità di Bose nel Biellese. Dopo il suo allontanamento aveva creato la Fraternità della Madia vicino a Ivrea

republika.title: Report, Procaccianti: FdI contento per i nuovi conduttori. A rischio inchieste di politica pre-voto
republika.description: L’inviato della trasmissione d’inchiesta contro la scelta della Rai di affidare il programma a Piervincenzi e Presutti

republika.title: Calciomercato chiuso. Gasp blocca Koné minacciando le dimissioni, Gudmundsson alla Lazio
republika.description: Si chiude alle 20: tutte le trattative in tempo reale

republika.title: Mosca sulla nomina di Fedorov al ministero della Difesa italiana: “Degna di una favola di Rodari”
republika.description: La portavoce del ministero degli Esteri russo, Maria Zakharova: “Ma non sono sicura che sarebbe più divertente della storia vera”. L’ex ministro ucraino nominato consulente per aiutare Roma su droni e contraerea. Crosetto: “Scelte pensando all’Italia non a Mosca, Kiev o Washington”

republika.title: Berrettini: “Minacce di morte dagli scommettitori”
republika.description: Il tennista romano racconta i messaggi ricevuti dal fratello al Roland Garros

npr.title: Nepal floods: Rescuers struggle to locate power plants to find trapped survivors
npr.description: Nearly a week after flash floods devastated parts of Nepal and Tibet, rescuers are still searching for people trapped in hydropower plants. But first they have to find the plants.

npr.title: SCOTUS allows Trump's ballroom project to continue. And, the Army secretary resigns
npr.description: The Supreme Court has ruled that President Trump's ballroom project may continue. And, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after 18 months on the job.

npr.title: Global finance ministers gather in North Carolina for G20 summit
npr.description: The U.S. is playing host to finance ministers from around the world this week. Russia's top economic official made a stir on Monday when he showed up in person at the meeting in North Carolina.

npr.title: The U.S. wants others to join its economic pressure campaign against Iran. Will they?

phys-org.title: Salt of the Earth: How Egypt's coastal sabkhas tell a story of climate and change
phys-org.description: Have you ever walked across a salt flat so expansive it feels like another planet? That's what it's like standing in Egypt's coastal sabkhas—those otherworldly landscapes where the ground crunches beneath your feet and the air shimmers with heat. These aren't just barren wastelands; they're living laboratories that record the pulse of our changing climate.

phys-org.title: Saturn encounter may have set distant centaur on path to becoming a comet
phys-org.description: More than 3 billion miles (4.8 billion kilometers) from Earth, an ancient icy object is slowly awakening. As it drifts inward through the solar system, the frozen body known as Centaur 450P/LONEOS has begun releasing gas and dust—behavior more commonly associated with comets than with centaurs, the small icy objects that typically orbit between Jupiter and Neptune.

phys-org.title: Canada's Labrador Shelf preserves climate records once thought erased by ice
phys-org.description: The Labrador Shelf is a shallow marine area on the margin of the Labrador Sea in the North Atlantic off the east coast of Canada. During the last ice age, this region was covered by the Laurentide Ice Sheet, one of the largest ice masses in Earth's history, which once covered vast parts of North America.

phys-org.title: A roadmap for animal-free chemical testing
phys-org.description: For many years, the European Union has pursued a policy aimed at the replacement, reduction and refinement of animal testing (the 3Rs principle). To put the ethical principle of the 3Rs into practice, the European Commission has published a roadmap for the gradual phaseout of animal testing in the safety assessment of chemicals.

phys-org.title: A sustainable flame retardant derived from corn steep liquor
phys-org.description: Certain phosphorus compounds are highly effective at suppressing fires, which is why they are widely used in flame retardants. Phosphorus, however, is a finite resource. Estimates suggest it could be depleted within the next 50–300 years. That is why, as part of the ScaleAmP project, a research team is working to extract phosphorus from corn steep liquor, a byproduct of starch production.

phys-org.title: Ocean heat waves linked with poorer health among children in coastal communities
phys-org.description: Marine heat waves—periods of abnormally warm ocean temperatures—may have negative health effects on children who live in coastal communities in low- and middle-income countries, according to a study led by researchers at Penn State and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

phys-org.title: AI-informed AdaptiveFlow redefines large-scale cloud computing for drug discovery
phys-org.description: Researchers today announced AdaptiveFlow, an AI-informed platform that can virtually screen billions of drug-like molecules with a 1,000-fold reduction in computational costs over existing methods. Developed and validated by scientists from St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, University of Pavia, Dana Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School, AdaptiveFlow allows prohibitively expensive ultra-large virtual drug screens to be conducted routinely. phys-org.description: When the ESA Earth observation mission FLEX launches into space on September 15, 2026, as scheduled, it will carry high-precision optical components from Jena, Germany. Researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Optics and Precision Engineering IOF have developed and manufactured a silicon-based double-slit assembly as well as two high-precision mirrors for the spectrometer on board the satellite. phys-org.title: Larger catalyst batches could make carbon recycling cheaper and easier to scale
phys-org.description: Turning carbon dioxide into industrial chemicals used in everything from synthetic fuels to plastics and pharmaceuticals is costly. But new research shows it does not have to be.

phys-org.title: Tests reveal how thermoplastic composites lose strength at elevated temperatures
phys-org.description: Researchers from Skoltech together with colleagues from Xi'an Jiaotong University and the Blagonravov Institute of Mechanical Engineering of the Russian Academy of Sciences, have conducted a systematic study of the flexural properties of pultruded glass fiber composites based on three different thermoplastic matrices: polyphenylene sulfide (PPS), polyamide-6 (PA6) and polypropylene (PP).

phys-org.title: Warmer waters, pest species and habitat loss major threats to small, rare freshwater fish
phys-org.description: One of Australia's most comprehensive assessments of endemic, rare or threatened freshwater fish has found numerous species are at severe risk of extinction because of multiple threats, including habitat loss, invasive species and warmer waters.

phys-org.title: Watching nanoparticles form in real time uncovers 'missing link' in microwave-assisted manufacturing
phys-org.description: Advanced materials power everything from batteries and electronics to clean energy technologies. For years, engineers have known that microwave-assisted synthesis can dramatically accelerate the chemical reactions used to manufacture these materials. Now, researchers at Carnegie Mellon University have provided new evidence challenging a long-held assumption about why, suggesting that microwaves speed chemical reactions in a fundamentally different way than many scientists believed.

phys-org.title: Where people go shapes urban mixing more than where they live, research finds
phys-org.description: For millennia, people have been drawn to cities for opportunities, jobs and the possibility of sharing a sidewalk with diverse and interesting groups of people.

phys-org.title: Cannabis ads may shape viewers' expectations about cannabis and sex
phys-org.description: Alcohol advertisers have long faced industrywide guidelines discouraging them from linking drinking with sexual success. Cannabis marketers have no comparable industrywide guidelines and may promote cannabis in connection with sex and intimacy. A new Washington State University study suggests such messages may influence young adults' intentions to use cannabis before sex, with potential implications for sexual decision-making and consent.

phys-org.title: What is public interest technology? An expert on data and policy explains how it helps people in need
phys-org.description: Every year, millions of people who qualify for food assistance never get it. The money exists and they meet the eligibility rules, but they don't know that the program exists or whether they qualify. For others, the application is too long and complicated.

phys-org.title: In tune with nature: Human speech follows a rhythm that is also found in the animal kingdom
phys-org.description: The temporal structure of speech rhythms resembles that of the communication signals of numerous animal species. This is shown by a study conducted by a research team from the Leibniz Center for General Linguistics (ZAS) in Berlin, Humboldt Universität zu Berlin, the University of Regensburg and the Institute for Advanced Studies at Aix-Marseille University.

phys-org.title: Martian astronomy: Percy sees a 'Phobos eclipse' from Mars
phys-org.description: What's so special about spotting Phobos crossing in front of the sun? Sure. It's just another image of Phobos crossing the disk of the sun, as seen from the surface of Mars. Like so much of the modern space era, these images, once amazing, are now almost routine. But there's some real science behind tasking the Mars rovers to conduct a little "Martian astronomy."

phys-org.title: Hidden protein recycling hubs discovered inside human sperm cells
phys-org.description: Researchers at VIB, VUB and the Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology (UK) have discovered a hidden feature of human sperm cells. Using advanced imaging technologies, they discovered specialized compartments within the sperm nucleus packed with proteasomes, which are responsible for breaking down and recycling proteins.

arxiv-ai.title: Time Capsule of Testable Human Knowledge: 41 Years of Jeopardy! in a Single Free Local Model
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2608.27459v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In 2011, IBM's Watson was something like a sealed capsule of its era's queryable knowledge. Its DeepQA system defeated the strongest human Jeopardy! champions, but the knowledge that let it do so lived in a curated billion-document corpus running on a cluster of POWER7 servers, frozen at build time and impossible to move or copy. We show that the same kind of artifact, a snapshot of what a culture can answer, is now portable and essentially free.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

proj-syn.title: Trump and Xi Should Align on AI
proj-syn.description: When potential outcomes are systemic and irreversible, preparation must precede certainty. This is the logic behind insurance, as well as every pandemic plan and arms-control treaty ever created, and it must be the principle that guides our approach to AI—beginning at the upcoming US-China summit.

proj-syn.title: The Quiet Revolution in Services
proj-syn.description: While economists debate whether industrialization can still play its traditional growth-promoting role in the current global and technological context, services have unexpectedly become an engine for economic development around the world. For developing and developed economies alike, the timing could not be better.

proj-syn.title: AI Addicts Won’t Make Better Workers
proj-syn.description: Economists widely agree that AI will boost labor productivity. But this view does not account for the possibility that hyperscalers will go all out to get people hooked on LLMs, because the narrower applications for which these tools are actually useful do not justify the massive investments made so far.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Crime Tax
proj-syn.description: Even excluding lives lost, communities displaced, and families ravaged, the economic costs of organized crime in the region produce a bleak picture, shaving 0.5–2 percentage points off annual GDP growth in the most affected countries. That, too, represents a hefty human toll.

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.

proj-syn.title: Gen Z Is Transforming South Asia
proj-syn.description: Facing diminished economic prospects, many young people see not flawed institutions in need of gradual reform, but predatory systems robbing them of their future. Across South Asia, this sense has animated powerful protest movements, some of which could shape their countries' political trajectories for decades to come.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.
